title: Invasive Vine Removal at Sligo Creek

sponsor.name: Chesapeake Climate Action Network / Action Fund

description:
Join CCAN and Friends of Sligo Creek to remove Invasive Vines along Sligo Creek in Hyattsville, MD.

We will meet along Sligo Creek (exact GPS coordinates will be emailed to participants) at 9am and work until about 11am. We will focus on non-native invasive vines including porcelainberry (Ampelopsis glandulosa var. brevipedunculata), English ivy (Hedera helix), and Kudzu (pueraria montana). Native Virginia creeper and poison ivy are also present and beneficial, so we will avoid those.

Please wear long pants, long sleeves, and close-toed shoes. Instructions and tools will be provided, so just bring yourself and a good attitude!

A reminder email will be sent out the day before with detailed instructions on where to meet.

title: ❤️ Oh Yes, You Can: Autism-Powered Activism Training with Chaz Stevens
description:
## **Event Description:**

Forget performative activism—hashtags don’t win battles. Diagnosed with autism at 57, Chaz Stevens turned his neurodivergence into a strategic powerhouse, forcing politicians like Florida’s Gov. Ron DeSantis into embarrassing policy reversals.

Remember Ron's insipid book ban?  Weakened by the Gov, with a finger pointed right at Chaz.

Writes Brendan Farrington of The Associated Press: "DeSantis backtracked on the 2022 law, narrowing its focus.  When his office was asked for examples of liberal activists abusing the law, only one name was provided: Chaz Stevens, a South Florida resident who has often lampooned government."

In this direct, provocative session, Chaz teaches you:

* How to **harness autistic literalism** to expose hypocrisy.
* Autism-optimized power mapping to strategically target decision-makers.
* Crafting clear, precise media messages to force measurable outcomes.

Stop tweeting. Start winning. Your autism isn’t holding you back—it’s your strongest asset.

**Are you ready to disrupt—and actually win?**

## **Who This Event Is For:**

This event is ideal for autistic individuals and allies ready to embrace bold, strategic activism to drive real and lasting change. Whether you identify as neurodivergent or you support the community, you're welcome here—provided you're ready to take impactful, measurable action.

**Note:** If you're more comfortable with slow, gentle activism, this training probably isn’t for you.

## **Important Note (Respect to the Autism Community):**

I mean no disrespect to the autism community—quite the opposite. My training explicitly values autistic strengths, recognizing that our literal thinking, precision, and meticulous attention to detail offer unique, powerful advantages for creating genuine change. My approach is bold and unconventional, but it’s built entirely upon deep respect for neurodivergent capabilities.

## **Personal Note from Chaz:**

What I've achieved—forcing real political reversals, exposing governmental hypocrisy—is entirely thanks to my neurodivergent perspective. My autism diagnosis at 57 came from a casual, passing comment by a PsyD who assumed I already knew—I absolutely did not. I spent my entire life disappointed... I never understood why I was different, why I didn't fit in, why social situations were entirely confusing. I didn't hate myself; I was just eternally frustrated.

Discovering my autism felt exactly like those videos where someone puts on chroma glasses and sees the color red clearly for the first time: instantly transformative, intensely emotional, and profoundly empowering.

It is my superpower—feel free to call me Clark Kent. I wouldn't change a single thing about my journey. Autism gave me the ability to disrupt systems and force real, measurable change.

## **Special Thanks:**

There’s nothing else like this training—and my deepest gratitude goes to Broward Democratic Party Executive Director **Christina Disbrow** for having the courage to support building a community of folks, both advantaged, and disadvantaged, by autism.

Together, friends, we can disrupt the heck outta the status quo.

## **Event Structure (60 minutes):**

* **45–50 min:** Interactive training session with real-world case studies, hands-on autism-optimized power mapping exercises, and precise media messaging practice.
* **10–15 min:** Interactive Q/A session.

## **Accessibility:**

Accommodations, including sensory-friendly options, closed captioning, and materials in alternative formats, are available. Please contact us directly at disrupt[at]revolt.training to discuss your specific needs.

## ⏰ Act Now—Reserve Your Spot

Spots are limited—sign up today to transform frustration into meaningful victories.

> *“Chaz doesn’t just push the envelope; he sets it on fire to make his point.”*

- Anna Eskamani, Florida State Representative

**Ready to disrupt and win?** Join us now.

Dr. T. Chaz Stevens has spent decades forcing political accountability, humiliating corrupt politicians, and engineering real-world change. His disruptive strategies are bold, effective, and battle-tested.

title: Hometown Fightback Community Conversations: Impacts of Medicaid and SNAP Cuts
description:
The Big Ugly Bill has passed the house and now is the time to make your voice heard. The bill calls for devastating cuts to Medicaid, SNAP, and the safety net, all to pay for tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy. Pennsylvania voters, like voters in other states, strongly support these programs, and with good reason. Medicaid provides critical support for millions of Pennsylvanians.

While new requirements for the state to help pay for the SNAP program would result in new expenditures for the state of $226 million to over a billion. The bill does all this harm while adding $2.4 trillion to the federal deficit.

This event is open to everyone. Join Pennsylvanians Together and the Pennsylvania Policy Center, for a real conversation about proposals that could harm Pennsylvanians, and what we can do about them. The Phoenixville Dems will be setting up a table at the Juneteenth celebrations in Phoenixville!

Juneteenth National Freedom Day illuminates the fact that slaves celebrated the abolishment of slavery with excitement and great joy. It is a reminder to all Americans of the status and importance of Americans of African descent as American citizens. For more than 140 years, Juneteenth National Freedom Day has been the oldest African American holiday observed in the United States.

Juneteenth celebrations began in Phoenixville in 2002, experienced a hiedas and returned in to our community in 2021 with a week-long series of virtual events that were educational, entertaining, and inspirational!

This year on Sunday, June 22, between 2 and 6 pm, the Phoenixville Juneteenth Committee (Black Light Projects , Diversity In Action, Orion Communities, The Colonial Theatre, and the Phoenixville Community Health Foundation) has organized a special collection of activities to engage the community and shed light on the importance of African American history in the United States and our community. We will commemorate this important date with historical re-enactors, music, art, dance, drummers, street theater, magic, Soul food, and storytelling. The events will take place on the 200 block of Bridge Street in Phoenixville.

What are we fighting for? 

	No kings is a national call to action and mass mobilization in response to the increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption of the Trump administration. We the people do not condone using important tax dollars for Trump to throw himself a birthday party. We do not support Trump using the military as a pawn in his political game. We stand united against kings since 1776 to today. 


What do we bring?

	The goal is to be comfortable for the one hour we plan to be demonstrating. Please use your best judgement on what would be appropriate for this peaceful event. Some ideas of what could make it on your packing list to bring:  a friend, your family, a sign that shows why you are attending(slogan ideas to follow), a water source, a lawn chair.

Where should we park?
	
	Please use public parking along Main street and Buffalo street. If you know anyone in the neighborhood, you could ask to park at their house. If you are physically able, consider walking. 

Where are we meeting?
	
	We will congregate in front of the Marion Town Hall and will populate the corner of Main Street/Buffalo Street. We will not block any streets or sidewalks. All roadways and walkways will remain accessible and open. No businesses will be blocked including any buildings we may find ourselves in front of. Please be mindful of making room for others using the public space who are not a part of this demonstration.

Among the group we encourage you to share your story, share with others why you're here or why this is important to you or for the town of Marion. We aren't gathering just to stand against oligarchy, we are building community and that takes vulnerability. If you feel awkward or embarrassed, please know you're not the only one! Showing up takes guts and humility. Being afraid is the first step to being brave and your courage will not go unnoticed by your community! We are stronger together. 

Following the protest we encourage you to shop Main street, visit the park or cemetery or stop into the Marion Public Library prior to our demonstration. Enjoy what Marion has to offer,  we want to make a statement of investing into our community!

What if this event escalates negatively? 

	Our event organizers will participate in training that will help them mitigate any negative incidents. The most important thing to remember is that you cannot control anyone's actions but your own. Remain peaceful, do not engage with counter-protesters, and follow the directions and leadership of event organizers. 

	Interested protesters can attend a Know Your Rights Training hosted by the ACLU. This online training is open to the public and will happen on June 10th at 7 pm.  Use this Link or copy this web address into your web browser to register. 

https://act.aclu.org/a/2025-kyr-training-2?/utm_source=email&source=nokingshostemail

No Kings Since 1776
Marion says No Kings!
The People United Can Never be Defeated
Oligarchy (with an X through the word) 
Money for Medicaid not Parades
For Democracy! No Kings.
Liberty and Justice for ALL

title: Speak to Denton County Commissioners about Vote Centers
description:

title: Nationwide Rise for Freedom Training Series – DEBRIEF CALL -1 hr.
description:
Thank you for being part of the Rise for Freedom Training Series! 

Let’s come together to reflect, connect, and imagine what’s next. 

Join the Rise for Freedom Training Series Debrief Call on Thursday, June 12th at 8-10 pm ET/7-9 pm CT/ 6-8 pm MT/5-7 pm PT!

On this debrief call, we will:

- Reflect on what resonated most from the training series
- Share feedback on what worked well and what could be improved
- Connect in breakout groups led by volunteers and partners to build community in individual states and regions
- Discuss what your community needs now to keep organizing
- Dream big about what’s possible next in this movement
- Talk about what Rise4Freedom is planning now and what you think our next steps should be. For example, should there be an in-person training like this series in your state or town this summer?

Whether you attended one session or all of them, your voice matters. Help us grow stronger together.

We’re so grateful to the incredible partners, speakers, facilitators, and production crew who made this series possible, and to YOU for showing up. 

Over the past 11 weeks, we held 10 powerful training sessions (plus a launch call) to equip communities with the tools to organize for inclusive democracy and push back against rising autocracy. These sessions covered everything from strategic outreach to broadcast and social media storytelling, with topics including:

- How to run a successful in-person training meeting
- Intro to organizing under creeping autocracy
- Building to a critical mass locally
- How to talk to people you might disagree with
- Harnessing our power to end political violence and repression
- De-escalation and action security
- Mutual aid & structures for stronger local organizing
- Strategic escalation: Choosing your tactics
- Digital hygiene deep training
- Broadcast and social media storytelling

description:
Gorman Heritage Farm is an educational farm in Evendale, north of Cincinnati, where they also operate a small CSA distribution.  We've been invited, *every other Friday*,  during the harvest season to glean anything not going to the CSA and distribute it nearby.  

Sign up for one or more gleaning shifts. We will be here gleaning **every other Friday** during the harvest season, but *you must register to get a spot.* (Please, do not simply show up at the farm if you have not registered. We can only accommodate registered volunteers.)

Gleaning involves harvesting food that will not go to market, but is still good food. We then get it distributed right away to a local hunger relief recipient.

The work will happen in the farm's fields in a variety of weather. It may involve bending/stooping, pulling, digging, some heavy lifting, and generally getting dirty.  There will also be some walking to the field sites.  This will vary each time.

**Registered volunteers will receive specific instructions about where to meet at the farm.**
